newsitem.title: USA: WorldCom, MFS Communications in $14 billion merger.
newsitem.headline: WorldCom, MFS Communications in $14 billion merger.

text.p: WorldCom Inc said early on Monday it and MFS Communications Co Inc had agreed to merge in a stock swap worth at least $14 billion, creating a giant international business communications company.

WorldCom said in a statement from its Jackson, Miss., headquarters that the merger agreement was unanimously approved by the boards of each company. Shareholders will vote on the deal at special meetings.

The merger with the Omaha, Neb.-based MFS will create a major business communications company providing "a single source for a full range of local, long distance, Internet and international service over an advanced fiber optic network," the statement said.

The merger comes only weeks after MFS's $2 billion purchase of UUNET Technologies Inc was completed Aug 12. That merger created a single source for Internet, voice, data and video services over an international fiber optic grid.
Each share of MFS common stock will be exchanged for 2.1 shares of WorldCom common stock.
"As of Friday's closing, the merger consideration for MFS stock is approximately $14 billion," the statement said.
The combined company will be known as MFS WorldCom.

Bernard J. Ebbers, president and chief executive of WorldCom, will become president and chief executive of MFS WorldCom. MFS chairman and chief executive James Crowe will become the chairman of the merged company.
The companies hope to close the merger in four to eight months.
The merged company will have current annualized revenue of about $5.4 billion, with more than 500,000 business customers throughout North America, Europe and Asia.
The combined company's board of directors will consist of an odd number of directors with WorldCom designating one more director than MFS.
The merger also is subject to federal regulatory approval.
